interest: This document provides valuable insight into the administrative tracking and diplomatic channels governing protected maritime vessels and civilian/diplomatic repatriation during World War II. It illustrates the role of Spain as the protecting power representing Japanese interests in the United States, specifically in communicating Japanese designations of hospital ships under international humanitarian law and facilitating early proposals for civilian and diplomatic personnel exchanges.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing documents filed under decimal classification 894.24 / 894.241 concerning Japanese army transports and hospital ships. The docket sheet records two wartime communications: a January 28, 1942 letter from the Navy Department transmitting British Admiralty intelligence concerning Japanese hospital ship designations alongside a January 6 Spanish Embassy memorandum proposing an exchange of Japanese and American personnel, and a December 7 communication from the Spanish Embassy enclosing a memorandum regarding Japan's designation of six additional hospital ships.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet listing correspondence regarding Japanese hospital ships and a proposal for American-Japanese personnel exchange.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, indexes State Department records filed under Army Transports - Japan. It summarizes a January 28, 1942 report from the Navy Department relaying British Admiralty information regarding Japanese hospital ships and enclosing a Spanish Embassy memorandum of January 6 proposing an exchange of Japanese and American personnel. It additionally records a December 7 communication from the Spanish Embassy transmitting a memorandum concerning the notification and use of six additional hospital ships by the Japanese Government.
